title: DynaSpace smartphone PPS validation profile
citation: Roussel, A., et al. (2025). Using Android Smartphones to Collect Precise Measures of Reaction Times to Multisensory Stimuli. Sensors, 25(19), 6072.
notes: Smartphone/DynaSpace audio-tactile PPS validation profile. The profile encodes the reported left-hemispace looming trajectory, fixed 640 cm comparator, six tactile timing anchors, no-vibration catch trials, and 72 recorded-trial distribution from the paper and app source. Bundled preload WAVs are toolkit-generated DynaSpace-style Gaussian white-noise burst trains rendered with the PPS Toolkit FABIAN/SOFA path; the original Android bursttrain WAVs are recorded as provenance but not redistributed.

reference_parameters.paper_role: smartphone methods validation using an audio-tactile PPS-style looming versus fixed-source task
reference_parameters.stimulus_asset_policy: The public PPS Toolkit profile does not redistribute the Android app's raw WAVs. The preload catalog bakes 44.1 kHz toolkit-generated DynaSpace-style burst-train sources through the existing FABIAN/SOFA renderer so the profile remains runnable and publication-safe.
reference_parameters.original_audio_engine: Max/MSP Spat with LISTEN HRTFs for source creation, then Android Oboe playback in the DynaSpace app
reference_parameters.toolkit_audio_engine: PPS Toolkit 3DTI-compatible Python SOFA/FABIAN reference renderer
reference_parameters.toolkit_source_type: Gaussian white-noise burst-train dry source rendered through FABIAN/SOFA
reference_parameters.source_asset_equivalence: trajectory, condition logic, 33-burst temporal structure, and approximate 95 ms burst spacing are matched; exact Android noise seed, Spat/LISTEN renderer, room response, phone transducer response, and motor mechanics are not bit-matched

stimulus_generation_operating_protocol.decision: Adopt the DynaSpace/Hobeika burst-train dry source as the smartphone-profile source profile while delegating spatialization to the 3DTI/SOFA renderer.
evidence_basis: Raw DynaSpace WAV audit detected 33 bursts with about 95 ms median inter-onset interval.
Hobeika lineage reports Gaussian white-noise bursts with 30 ms duration, 10 ms rise/fall, and 65 ms inter-burst interval.
Consensus searches supported broadband onset transients for localization/salience and supported HRTF/ILD/ITD/reverb/near-field cues as renderer-level spatial properties.
Consensus searches warned that rising intensity alone can produce looming salience, so matched-level controls remain necessary for causal inference.
stimulus_generation_operating_protocol.spatialization_policy: Render HRTF, ILD, ITD, near-field, distance attenuation, future trajectory angle, and optional room/DRR/IACC cues through 3DTI/SOFA rather than hard-coding them into the dry source.
stimulus_generation_operating_protocol.control_policy: Keep the DynaSpace replication contrast available, and add matched-level control variants for inference-focused future studies.

no_vibration_catch_code.semantic: auditory-only catch trial with no phone vibration

reference_parameters.primary_analysis_contrast: looming audio-tactile RT pattern compared with fixed-source audio-tactile RT pattern across matched vibration timing anchors
reference_parameters.baseline_policy: No tactile-only baseline is encoded for this profile because the smartphone task's main validation contrast is looming versus fixed sound with no-vibration catches.
reference_parameters.trajectory_override_policy: Future variants should change azimuth_start_deg and azimuth_end_deg together for another constant-bearing approach angle, or provide cartesian endpoints for curved or non-radial paths while preserving the same anchor-table logic.

provenance.source: Sensors 2025 article DOI 10.3390/s25196072 and PubMed PMID 41094896 identify the smartphone RT methods paper.
DynaSpace source repository at https://forge-2.ircam.fr/roussel/dynaspace/ contains the Android DynaSpaceIrcam app used for the task.
MainActivity.kt defines timeArray = [105, 1625, 2385, 2765, 2955, 3050, 0], with the zero value used as a no-vibration catch.
rand.cpp creates 48 recorded audio-tactile rows across two sound modes, six timing values, and four repeats, plus 24 no-vibration catch rows; five practice rows are prepended.
The Android raw assets bursttrainlooming.wav and bursttrainfixe.wav are stereo 48 kHz PCM_16 files with 184800 frames, i.e. 3.85 s duration.
WavAudioPlayer.cpp schedules phone vibration after the requested delay plus a 50 ms sleep offset and calls the Android vibrator for 60 ms when the delay is nonzero.
The PPS Toolkit public preload uses generated broadband proxy WAVs through the bundled FABIAN/SOFA renderer and records the original Android WAVs as non-redistributed provenance.
